name: fuel
description: A fast, self-iterating calorie/protein/weight tracker — Next.js PWA backed by Google Sheets, with AI estimation

paragraphs: A fast, self-iterating calorie / protein / weight tracker — a Next.js PWA backed by a Google Sheet, with AI estimation.

Every tracker I tried was slow, ad-heavy, and locked my data inside someone else's database. Fuel is the opposite: logging a meal is a single tap, the "database" is a Google Sheet I own and can export at any moment, and the interface quietly reorganizes itself around what I actually eat. It installs to the home screen and behaves like a native app — offline-tolerant, instant, no sign-in friction.
Personal project and proof-of-work. The seed catalog, weights, and goals are my own real usage data.
features: Food + quantity logging — each food is one canonical entry (per-100g or per-unit); the amount is chosen at log time, prefilled with the last amount you used. A 5-second Undo toast (and a "Logged twice — undo?" guard)…

AI calorie/protein estimation — describe anything ("burrito bowl with chicken") and a Gemini-backed route returns calories and protein you can tweak before logging. Estimates log as one-offs and become saved foods…
Gram-accurate foods — staples (yogurt, fruit, protein powder, …) are stored as per-100g macros with a default gram serving, so amounts are exact rather than guessed "servings."

Weekly glide path — daily weigh-ins are averaged Sunday–Saturday and judged PASS/FAIL against a fixed weekly target (−1.0 lb/week). The top of the screen always shows this week's average, the target, and the average you…

A self-iterating UI — the 12 Pinned foods are recomputed on each load from the distinct days you logged them in the last 14 days, so the things you reach for most stay one tap away — without the list churning under you.
